full_judgment:
Md. Abdul Wahhab Miah J. This appeal, by leave, is from the judgment and order dated the 4th day of March, 2009 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in First Miscellaneous Appeal No.162 of 1991 dismissing the appeal. 

 2. Short facts necessary to dispose this appeal are that respondent No.1 herein as the plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No.137 of 1986 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now the Joint District Judge), Second Court, Chittagong for specific performance of contract impleading the present petitioners and one Gour Shankar Banik as principal defendant Nos.1 and 2 and the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong as pro-forma defendant. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 25.02.1987. Thereafter, the appellant who was defendant No.1 (hereinafter referred to as the defendant) filed an application in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Second court, Chittagong under Order a, rule 13 and section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for setting aside the ex-parte decree alleging that the ex-parte decree was obtained by the plaintiff fraudulently without serving any summons upon him. He came to know about the ex-parte decree on 12.07.1987, when his daughter was resisted by the plaintiff from picking up guava from the guava tree situated on the bhiti of the suit land disclosing that he got the land by a decree from the said Court of the Subordinate Judge. The plain-tiff also threatened the defendant to leave the suit land, otherwise he could face serious consequences. On such disclosure of facts by the plaintiff, the defendant made an enquiry in the Court on 15.07.1987 and came to know definitely about the ex-parte decree and then filed the application for the relief aforementioned. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No.67 of 1987. 

 3. The plaintiff - respondent (hereinafter referred to as the plaintiff) contested the miscellaneous case by filing written objection asserting that summonses of the suit were duly served upon the defendants including defendant No.1 and the Court being satisfied as to the service of summons upon the defendants fixed the suit for ex-parte hearing and eventually the suit was decreed ex-parte. 

 4. At the time of hearing of the miscellaneous case, both the parties examined one witness each. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 26.06.1989 rejected the application on the finding, inter-alia, that the summons of the suit was duly served upon the defendant-petitioner on 19.09.1986 which was evidenced from the service returns of the summons. The process server gave a report to the effect that no having found the defendant present served the summons upon him personally by taking his signature. The learned Subordinate Judge further observed that since the summons of the suit was served upon defendant No.1 as per report of the process server, there could no be any doubt as t the service of summons of the suit upon him. The learned Subordinate Judge further observed that although the decree was passed against defendant Nos.1 and 2 defendant No.2 did not challenge the same by filing any miscellaneous case. The Court below further found that the application was barred by limitation as in support of the knowledge of the ex-parte decree of the suit by the defendant for the first time on 12.07.1987, no other witness was examined. 

 5. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, the defendant filed First Miscellaneous Appeal No.29 of 1989 before the then Sessions of the High Court Division at Chittagong which having been transferred to the permanent seat in Dhaka was renumbered as Miscellaneous Appeal No.162 of 1991. A Division Bench of the High Court Division hearing the appeal by the impugned judgment and order dismissed the same. Against the judgment and order of the High Court Division, the appellant filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.948 of 2009 before this Division and leave was granted by this Court giving rise to this appeal; the grounds are: 

 "I. For that having regard to the provisions of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the issue in an application for setting aside ex-parte decree being that the summons was not duly served on the defendant or that he was prevented by any sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called on for hearing, and there being evidence on record of the defendant as PW-1 in the Miscellaneous Case No.67 of 1987 that he did not receives the summons of the suit and that the signature of the summons signifying the service on him was not his, and having regard to the fact that his evidence in this respect was not at all controverted by the evidence of the process server or any other witness, the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the trial Court committed no illegality in rejecting the Miscellaneous case filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and in that view of the matter the High Court Division erred in law in not restoring the suit by allowing the FMA upon setting aside the ex-parte decree of the trial Court. 

 II. For that the plaint of the suit having shown the address of the defendant in a village at Mirersarai in Chittagong, and admittedly the summons, according to the process server's report, having been served at an address at Halishahar in Chittagong town which is given as the present address of the defendant "C/O: Dr. S.L. Muzumder, 557, Halishahar Road, Chatopol, P.S. Double Mooring, Chittagong" and the defendant in his deposition as P.W.1 in the Miscellaneous Case having categorically stated that he never lived at Halishahar, Chittagong and that did not know the witnesses named in the service return of the summons, the High Court Division erred in law in failing to hold that the summons of the defendant was not duly served and in that view of the matter the High Court Division was wrong in failing to hold that the defendant's evidence having satisfied that the summons was not served on him, the suit is liable to be restored upon setting aside the ex-parte decree and on such finding the FMA ought to have been allowed by the High Court Division." 

 9. It is by now a well settled legal principle that in case of allegation of non-service of summons made by the defendant, the onus is upon the plaintiff to prove the service of summons. In the instant case, admittedly the process server who allegedly served the summons upon the defendant was not examined. Not only was that none in whose presence the process server allegedly served the summons also examined. The plaintiff was examined as OPW 1. He stated in his cross-examination that he was not present when the summons was served upon the defendant. He further stated that the defendant did not sign the summons in his presence and that he did not know the persons who were present at the time of service of the summons (in the deposition sheet, in Bangla, it has been recorded as" 

 10. So, OPW1 cannot be accepted as a witness to the service of summons upon the defendant. In this regard, it is also necessary to state that OPW1 in his examination-in-chief stated that the defendant after coming from India used to live at Halishahar, Chittagong town (which fact was denied by PW 1) and the summons of the suit was served upon the plaintiff at his Halishahar address, so the onus was upon the plaintiff to prove that actually the defendant lived at Halishahar than his village address, but he failed to discharge the said onus. It further appears that in the plaint, two addresses of the defendant were shown, one his village address at village-Dewanpur, Upazila-Mirersharai, District-Chittagong and the other at 557, Halishahar Road, Chatopol, P.S. Double Mooring, Chittagong under the care of one Dr. S.L. Muzumder, but the summons of the suit was allegedly served at the address of Halishahar only, i.e. no summons was served at the village address of the defendant. It is also very pertinent to state that the suit property is in village-Dewanpur, Police Station -Mirersharai (as evident from the schedule to the plaint), so it was natural that the summons of the suit would be served at his village address. The defendant in his deposition categorically stated that it was not correct that he used to stay at Halishahar, Chittagong town and that his house was not at Halishahar. None was examined from Halishahar to prove that the defendant actually lived at Halishahar address. In this regard, it is also very important to state that the defendant in his application under Order IX, rule 13 mentioned only one address, i.e. village-Dewanpur , Upazila-Mirersharai, so it was more obligatory upon the plaintiff to show that the defendant actually used to live at Halishahar under the care of one Dr. S.L Muzumder, 557, Halishahar Road, Chatopol, P.S. Double Mooring in which address the summons of the suit was allegedly served. Our common sense failed to see any reason to mention an address of the defendant in the plaintiff under the care of some body in a town, when the suit property is situated in a village. And then again why the summons of the suit should be served at the temporary address in the care of some body without serving the summons at the permanent village address where the suit property is situated and this speaks a volume and lends prima-facie support to the case of the defendant that the ex-parte decree was obtained fraudulently without serving any summon upon him, but neither the learned Subordinate Judge not the High Court Division considered these apparent factual and legal aspect of the case and thus fell into an error in taking an erroneous decision in rejecting the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code.
